transcript:
[Doctor]: Good morning, Ms. Mitchell. I’m Dr. Smith. How are you doing today?

[Patient]: Good morning, Dr. Smith. I’m doing well, thank you.

[Doctor]: I understand you’re here because of a possible exposure to COVID-19. Could you tell me a bit more about that?

[Patient]: Yes, I was informed that I had been in contact with someone who tested positive for COVID-19 recently. So, I wanted to get checked out.

[Doctor]: I see. When did this contact happen?

[Patient]: It was about three days ago.

[Doctor]: And since then, have you experienced any symptoms such as fever, cough, shortness of breath, or loss of taste or smell?

[Patient]: No, I haven’t had any symptoms at all.

[Doctor]: That’s good to hear. Have you noticed any fatigue, chills, or other unusual symptoms?

[Patient]: No, none of those either.

[Doctor]: Any gastrointestinal symptoms like nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea?

[Patient]: No, my stomach has been fine.

[Doctor]: How about headaches or muscle aches?

[Patient]: No headaches or muscle pain.

[Doctor]: Great. And any new allergies or immune-related symptoms?

[Patient]: No, nothing new.

[Doctor]: All right, thank you for providing all that information. I see from your records that you have a history of mild asthma. Is that correct?

[Patient]: Yes, I have mild asthma. It’s usually well-controlled.

[Doctor]: Are you currently taking any medications for your asthma or any other conditions?

[Patient]: I have an albuterol inhaler that I use when needed, but I haven’t needed it recently.

[Doctor]: Okay, and any seasonal allergies you're dealing with at the moment?

[Patient]: Just the usual, but nothing out of the ordinary.

[Doctor]: Good to know. Since you’re currently asymptomatic, we won’t need to do a physical examination today. However, it’s important to monitor for any symptoms that might develop.

[Patient]: Understood.

[Doctor]: Have you been tested for COVID-19 already?

[Patient]: Yes, I had an RT-PCR test done yesterday. I’m still waiting for the results.

[Doctor]: That’s good. While we wait for the results, it’s crucial to take some precautions. First, I recommend that you self-isolate for 14 days from the date of exposure to prevent any potential spread.

[Patient]: Okay, I can do that.

[Doctor]: During this period, please monitor yourself for any symptoms, such as fever, cough, shortness of breath, or loss of taste or smell. If you develop any symptoms, you can take over-the-counter medications as needed.

[Patient]: What kind of medications should I take if I get symptoms?

[Doctor]: For fever or pain, you can take Acetaminophen 500 mg orally every 6 hours as needed, but not for more than 3 days.

[Patient]: Got it. I’ll make sure to have that on hand.

[Doctor]: Perfect. I’ve also scheduled a telehealth appointment for you in 5 days to review your test results and check if you’ve developed any symptoms.

[Patient]: That sounds good.

[Doctor]: In the meantime, maintain good hydration, proper nutrition, and get plenty of rest. Also, if you experience any severe symptoms like difficulty breathing or persistent chest pain, seek urgent care immediately.

[Patient]: I will. Thank you for the advice.

[Doctor]: Lastly, continue practicing preventive measures such as wearing a mask, hand hygiene, and social distancing, especially if you need to be around others.

[Patient]: I’ve been doing that, and I’ll keep it up.

[Doctor]: Excellent. Do you have any questions or concerns about the plan we’ve discussed?

[Patient]: No, I think I understand everything. Thank you for your help.

[Doctor]: You’re welcome, Ms. Mitchell. Take care and stay safe. We’ll talk again in a few days.

[Patient]: Thank you, Dr. Smith. I will. Goodbye.

[Doctor]: Goodbye.
